strengths: The paper addresses a useful question for researchers in code representation learning and program analysis: how source code and natural-language supervision can improve representations used with low-level code alone. This provides an identifiable interested audience.

The reported results are promising within the evaluated setting. Function-name accuracy improves from 29.41 to 33.41, and summarization BLEU-4 improves from 32.43 to 34.36 over the strongest listed baselines for those metrics.

The high-level architecture is understandable, and evaluation covers both discriminative and generative tasks. Component ablations, comment comparisons, and the CodeT5 extension investigate relevant design choices.
The manuscript provides a Zenodo link for datasets, implementation, and configurations, alongside several experimental hyperparameters. These resources could support reproducibility.
weaknesses: Necessary—resolve the evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping POJ-104 labels across training, validation, and testing, while Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes. An ordinary classification head cannot learn the held-out classes through the stated training procedure. If this is actually retrieval, specify the training objective, candidate pool, ranking cutoff, and MAP/MAR/MAF1 definitions. This ambiguity affects the main results and most ablations. Also reconcile the statements that generation is evaluated on validation data in Section 3.2 and test data in Section 4.3, and document split construction and duplicate handling.

Necessary—align the binary-analysis claims with the inputs actually evaluated. The experiments use compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function, global, and type names. Such representations are not trivially interchangeable with stripped executable binaries, contrary to the introductory footnote. Specify compilation and normalization precisely, and either narrow the claims to the evaluated LLVM setting or provide evidence on representations obtained from stripped binaries. The 91-class function-name experiment also supports a narrower claim than unrestricted name recovery.

Necessary—separate the contribution of interpolation from additional training and changed objectives. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70. The assertion that PCL converged does not establish that downstream gains arise specifically from interpolation. Comparisons with matched training budgets and objectives, together with separate scalar and feature-wise interpolation ablations, are needed for the component-level claims in RQ3. Alternatively, restrict conclusions to the complete training procedure.

Necessary—qualify the conclusions about human-written comments. The collapse from 43.78 to 3.11 MAP in one POJ-104 experiment is striking, but comment extraction, sample matching, missing comments, truncation, and optimization behavior are insufficiently documented. Length distributions alone do not establish that verbosity, implementation detail, or stylistic variation caused the collapse. Moreover, removing synthetic comments reduces MAF1 by only 0.79 points. Provide controlled evidence and stability diagnostics, or report this as an observation specific to the tested data and configuration. The greater-than-97% multi-objective degradation in Section 5.3 likewise lacks sufficient experimental detail to support its general explanation.

Necessary—support or narrow the semantic-comprehension claims. BLEU/GLEU and exact match measure reference agreement rather than functional correctness or human usefulness. Clarify the provenance and quality of the apparently CodeT5-generated summarization references. The qualitative evidence also needs correction: Figure 7 treats 'Unloads a mutex' as successful while dismissing GraphCodeBERT's essentially equivalent 'Unloads the mutex'; Figure 8 displays 'status <<' without an operand in both the reference and generated code. Compilation/behavioral checks or independent human assessment could support stronger claims; otherwise, describe these results as textual reconstruction.

Necessary—make the implemented method reproducible from its description. Clarify whether interpolation always mixes source and comment embeddings, as Figure 2 and Section 2.4 suggest, or can mix any two modalities, as Algorithm 1 states. Figure 3 uses concatenation while Equations 8 and 10 use addition. Specify the actual encoder checkpoints, pooling and projection architecture, interpolation-network dimensions, temperature, pretraining hyperparameters, and whether gradients propagate through the binary-dependent targets in Equation 5.

Necessary—correct numerical reporting and temper performance claims. Section 5.1 reports MAF1 decreases of 2.07, 7.46, and 18.25 percentage points, but Table 7 implies 0.79, 2.85, and 6.97 points; the former values are relative percentages. Table 4 incorrectly assigns negative changes to PCL precision, recall, and F1 values that exceed RoBERTa's. Table 6 also shows lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT and only a 0.43-point exact-match improvement. Single-seed results without uncertainty estimates do not establish reliable superiority for such small differences.

Optional—shorten the repetitive human-learning analogies and distinguish empirical motivation from demonstrated mechanisms. Broader compiler and architecture coverage would strengthen practical applicability once the evaluated scope and central protocols are clear.
